headline: Dollar Tree beats with 4.6% comparable sales growth and raises its earnings outlook; shares jump 11%
takeaway: Traffic rose 3.8% and comparable sales 4.6%, above the top of the company’s range, and full-year earnings guidance went up. Profit margins fell because Dollar Tree is reinvesting tariff refunds in prices and stores, a one-off that also inflates the full-year outlook. The shares rose 11.2% to $154.65.
results: Total revenue rose 6.9% to $5.1 billion and comparable store sales 4.6%, with traffic up 3.8% and average ticket up 0.8%. Diluted earnings per share were $1.24 and adjusted $1.16, both including a $0.42 cost from reinvesting tariff refunds; operating margin contracted 110 basis points, including a 195-point hit from that reinvestment.

Dollar Tree opened 84 stores, converted or added about 800 stores to its multi-price format (now about 7,400 stores), and ended the quarter with 9,511 stores. It generated $375 million of operating cash flow and $122 million of free cash flow, and bought back $205 million of shares.
mgmt: Chief executive Mike Creedon said traffic accelerated to 3.8% and drove sales above the high end of the outlook, crediting a broader assortment, better stores and stronger customer engagement. He said the focus for the holiday season is to make Dollar Tree the destination for value, convenience and discovery.

The company raised its fiscal 2026 adjusted earnings per share outlook to $8.05–$8.25, which includes a benefit of about $0.65 from tariff refunds, and expects fourth-quarter comparable sales growth of 3–4% and adjusted earnings per share of $2.46–$2.66, including about $0.25 of cost from reinvesting those refunds.
view: The important number is traffic: 3.8% more shoppers is strong for a mature chain and shows the multi-price strategy, selling items above $1.25, is drawing customers rather than driving them away. That is why the shares jumped 11%, in a market rotating from chip stocks into consumer and defensive names.

The earnings figures need care. The full-year guidance includes about $0.65 per share of tariff refunds that will not repeat, while the quarter’s margins were held down by reinvesting those refunds. Strip both out and underlying profit growth is modest, held back by wage and freight costs.

At about 18–19 times earnings, Dollar Tree trades at a fair price for a business finally growing traffic after years of problems, and the sale of Family Dollar has made it simpler. I think the turnaround is real, but the valuation already reflects it; I would want to see margins expand without the help of tariff refunds before calling it cheap.
watch: Traffic in the holiday quarter, operating margin excluding tariff effects, and the pace of multi-price conversions.
